description: ES6+ JavaScript for real applications: destructuring, spread/rest, template literals, modules, closures, scope, `this`, and asynchronous JavaScript with Promises and async/await.

lessons.title: Scope and Hoisting
lessons.description: Understand where JavaScript variables are visible and why declarations behave differently depending on whether you use var, let, or const.
lessons.originalIntent: Understand where JavaScript variables are visible and why declarations behave differently depending on whether you use var, let, or const.

lessons.title: Closures
lessons.description: Understand how functions can remember variables from the scope where they were created, and use that behavior to build private state and reusable behavior.
lessons.originalIntent: Understand how functions can remember variables from the scope where they were created, and use that behavior to build private state and reusable behavior.

lessons.title: The this Keyword
lessons.description: Learn why this is determined by how a regular function is called, how method calls differ from plain function calls and arrow functions, and how to avoid losing the intended this context in callbacks.
lessons.originalIntent: Learn why this is determined by how a regular function is called, how method calls differ from plain function calls and arrow functions, and how to avoid losing the intended this context in callbacks.

lessons.title: Destructuring and Spread
lessons.description: Practice destructuring values from arrays and objects and using spread syntax to expand or copy data concisely in modern JavaScript.
lessons.originalIntent: Practice destructuring values from arrays and objects and using spread syntax to expand or copy data concisely in modern JavaScript.

lessons.title: Array Methods
lessons.description: Use map, filter, reduce, and find to transform, select, aggregate, and locate data declaratively instead of rebuilding every operation with manual loops.
lessons.originalIntent: Use map, filter, reduce, and find to transform, select, aggregate, and locate data declaratively instead of rebuilding every operation with manual loops.

lessons.title: Modules and Imports
lessons.description: Practice using ES modules to split JavaScript into reusable files with explicit imports and exports, and learn to diagnose default-versus-named export mistakes.
lessons.originalIntent: Practice using ES modules to split JavaScript into reusable files with explicit imports and exports, and learn to diagnose default-versus-named export mistakes.

lessons.title: Promises
lessons.description: Understand how Promises represent future asynchronous results, work with pending, fulfilled, and rejected states, and chain asynchronous operations with then and catch.
lessons.originalIntent: Understand how Promises represent future asynchronous results, work with pending, fulfilled, and rejected states, and chain asynchronous operations with then and catch.

lessons.title: Async and Await
lessons.description: Use async functions and await to write Promise-based asynchronous code in a readable, sequential style while preserving the underlying Promise model.
lessons.originalIntent: Use async functions and await to write Promise-based asynchronous code in a readable, sequential style while preserving the underlying Promise model.

lessons.title: Error Handling
lessons.description: Practice handling failures in synchronous and asynchronous JavaScript with try/catch and Promise catch, while making sure error handling provides useful recovery or user-facing feedback.
lessons.originalIntent: Practice handling failures in synchronous and asynchronous JavaScript with try/catch and Promise catch, while making sure error handling provides useful recovery or user-facing feedback.

lessons.title: Modern JavaScript Challenge
lessons.description: Build a small realistic JavaScript feature that combines closures, array methods, ES modules, async/await, and deliberate error handling into one coherent application.
lessons.originalIntent: Build a small realistic JavaScript feature that combines closures, array methods, ES modules, async/await, and deliberate error handling into one coherent application.
